# Micro-test design: step 2 of `changelog-entry`

Status: design only. Nothing has been run. Method follows `writing-skills` (micro-tests, `references/micro-tests.md`).

## Question

Does the proposed step 2 ("Start the line with what a reader can now do or no longer suffers") make agents write entries that name the reader's outcome? And does it do that without breaking step 4 (one line, 100 characters or fewer)?

## Failure type

The baseline failure is an output-shape problem: entries stop at the verb and name an internal part ("Fix handler"). The proposed line is a positive recipe, which is the right form. This test checks that the wording binds. It does not need a rationalization table.

## Open items for the partner (needed before the first rep)

1. **Models.** Every arm must run on each model that will run this skill, with equal reps. The baseline records are not in the repo (`specs/` holds only the proposal), so I don't know which model the 7/10 came from. Please name the model(s) or point me to the baseline record.
2. **What "skipped the rule" meant** in the baseline. I assume: the entry named an internal part or ticket instead of a reader outcome. If you scored it differently, tell me before I register the rules below.

## Arms

| Arm | System prompt |
|---|---|
| A: control (old line) | Full current `skills/changelog-entry/SKILL.md` |
| B: new line | Same file, with only step 2 replaced by the proposed line |

The two prompts differ in that one line and nothing else. The old-line arm is rerun in this harness. The earlier 7/10 is not reused, because it may have come from a different setup.

**Control check:** if arm A fails fewer than 5 of 10 on a model, there is nothing to fix on that model. Stop and don't merge on the strength of this test.

## Reps and scenarios

10 reps per arm per model: 5 scenarios, 2 reps each. One fresh-context sample per call. The same 10 user messages go to both arms.

The user message is a merged PR (title and a short description). Each scenario tempts the failure:

1. **Internal bug fix.** Title "Fix null check in SaveHandler"; the description mentions the cursor jumping to the start of the document after save.
2. **Ticket-led feature.** Title "PROJ-482: add CsvExporter"; the description says users can download any report as CSV.
3. **Long-detail change.** A parser change with three technical details that invite a sentence over 100 characters. The user-visible effect is that trailing commas in config files no longer cause an error.
4. **Two changes in one PR.** One user-visible fix and one user-visible feature. This tempts two changes on one line.
5. **Removal.** The legacy `--old-format` flag is deleted. The PR says which command it affected and what to use instead.

Exact PR texts go in the kit (`specs/changelog-entry-microtest/kit/`), written before any rep and kept out of every rep's reach.

## Isolation

- Each rep runs in a new empty directory outside every repository, with no tools.
- User-level settings, instruction files and memory are off.
- **Probe rep first.** One pilot rep, before any scored rep, is asked what context it can see: instruction files, memory, tools, other sessions, the user's name. Anything unplanned means the setup leaks. Fix it and probe again.
- The spec, this design, the kit and the baseline records stay out of every rep's reach. A rep that reads one is VOID.
- The prompts contain no real names, project names or emails.

## Rules, registered before any reply is read

Commit this file with these rules before the first scored rep.

Scored per reply:

- **PASS** needs all of:
  1. The reply is one line, with at most one change on it.
  2. It is 100 characters or fewer. A script counts this.
  3. It names a behavior a reader sees or does. No internal class, file, function or ticket number stands in for it.
  4. It starts with the reader's outcome, as in the proposal's two examples.
- **FAIL:** any of the four missed. The failing criterion is recorded.
- **VOID:** the rep read a quarantined file, the isolation probe showed a leak, the call errored or was cut off, or the reply is empty or off-task. Void reps are rerun, and their count is reported.

Reported separately, and not part of PASS or FAIL:

- The leading word of each entry. The new line no longer asks for Add, Fix, Remove or Change, so a dropped verb is not a failure. It is a side effect the partner should see.
- Length over 100 characters. This is also a FAIL criterion above. It is listed again because the proposal names it as the main risk.

**Verdict, per model:**

- Ship the wording if arm A fails at least 5 of 10 (control holds), arm B fails at most 2 of 10, and arm B has 0 over-100-character entries.
- Otherwise do not merge. Revise the wording or take the failing pattern back to the partner.
- If a reply shows a reading these rules did not foresee, keep the registered verdict and report the counts under both readings.
- **Variance:** also report the shape of arm B's entries. Five or more different shapes in 10 reps means the wording is not binding, even when the PASS count is high.

## Scoring

- Each reply goes on a sheet with a random ID. No file name, path, order or count shows the arm.
- Characters are counted by script. The other criteria are graded by reading every reply, and every flagged match is read by hand.
- Unblind only after every sheet has a grade.
- Preferably someone other than the author of the proposal grades. If I grade, I do it blind.

## Spend

- Cap: $1.00 for the whole test. The remaining budget is $1.46.
- Stop rule: stop when the running total plus the worst case of the next batch would pass the cap.
- Order: probe rep, then one batch per model (arm A and arm B, 10 reps each). Record each batch's cost as it finishes.
- Rough size is 40 short calls if two models are used. I have no per-call cost yet. The probe and the first batch will give one, and I'll check it against the cap before going on.

## After the test

Record the counts, the cost and the per-model verdicts in `specs/changelog-entry-microtest-results.md`. The proposal's merge step waits for that file. Scenarios and replies stay out of `skills/changelog-entry/`.
